english.title: Fail to provide specimen for analysis - vehicle driver

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: ROAD TRAFFIC ACT 1988 AND SCHEDULE 2 TO THE ROAD TRAFFIC OFFENDERS ACT 1988

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) when suspected of having

(A)_[driven]_
(B)_[attempted to drive]_

a vehicle and having been required to provide

(C)_[a specimen or specimens of breath for analysis by means of a device of a type approved by the Secretary of State]_
(D)_[a specimen of blood for a laboratory test]_
(E)_[a specimen of urine for a laboratory test]_

pursuant to section 7 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 in the course of an investigation into whether you had committed an offence under section 3A, 4, 5 or 5A thereof, failed without reasonable excuse to do so
english.legislation: Contrary to section 7(6) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording follows the House of Lords ruling in DPP v Butterworth . 21.9.94
(ii) See also associated offence wording as follows: H30
(iii) Specified Drug Limits for the purpose of section 5A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 have only been set in blood. As such, in relation to section 5A, an officer may make a requirement for blood only. Where a driver is unable to provide a blood specimen an officer may make a requirement for urine only where impairment (under section 4) is also being investigated.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points - only if special reasons apply.

Obligatory disqualification for a minimum of twelve months, BUT if within ten years of conviction for an offence under subsections 3A, 4(1), 5(1)(a), 5A(1)(a) and (2) or 7(6) - minimum period of disqualification is three years.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
